title: Prompt Patterns That Reliably Improve Output

sections.subtitle: The four-part prompt
sections.description:
Most reliable prompts contain four pieces: role, context, task, and output format.

The format is not decoration. It tells the model what a successful answer looks like, which makes evaluation much easier.

visualization.title: The four-part prompt
visualization.html:
The four-part prompt

Role

You are a patient Python tutor.

Context

The reader knows loops but not decorators.

Task

Explain decorators with one example.

Format

Short answer, then a code block.

sections.subtitle: Few-shot examples
sections.description:
Examples are compressed instructions. Two or three high-quality examples usually beat a long paragraph of adjectives.

Keep examples consistent: same shape, same level of detail, same output format.

sections.subtitle: Evaluate, don't guess
sections.description:
Write down the failure modes you care about before you tune the prompt: hallucination, missing constraints, wrong format, or excessive length.

Then test the prompt against a small set of fixed examples. A prompt that feels better is not necessarily a prompt that performs better.
